research_questions.question: To what extent does feasibility-aware candidate ranking improve planning success under fixed simulation-validation budgets on unseen assemblies relative to ASAP variants under a common testbed?
At matched planning success, how close can the required number of validated candidate actions approach the one-successful-action-per-transition lower bound on unseen assemblies?
Which inference-time, pre-simulation features contribute predictive utility for removability, stability, joint feasibility, and downstream planning?

claim_scope.primary: unseen assemblies drawn from the frozen ASAP/Fusion 360 Gallery assembly split
not_primary_claims: unseen semantic product families, because family identities are unavailable
out-of-distribution geometry beyond the frozen source distribution
wall-clock superiority across different hardware or simulator implementations
future_extensions: few-shot adaptation to a separately collected target family
single-gripper robotic execution with explicit grasp and arm planning
selective simulation bypass after an independently validated risk-coverage study
a faster collision or physics backend

large.label_exploration: ASAP-compatible DFS with heur-out part ordering

exclusions.production_failure_reason: repeatable simulator SIGSEGV in production and retry; absent from the indexed dataset and ineligible for training or evaluation
exclusions.review_required_policy: include policy-review rows because their indexed files passed integrity checks; report them by tier and do not reinterpret them as corrupt
exclusions.orphan_checkpoint_policy: exclude all unreferenced state checkpoints; only candidate files named by an authoritative assembly summary are indexed

observed_profile.interpretation: complete_label_search_fraction describes label-generation coverage and is not a learned-planner result

prediction_problem.context: current remaining-part state and one simulator-proposed stable pose

R.name: directional removability
R.definition: whether the selected part separates successfully along the selected principal direction

T.name: post-removal stability
T.definition: whether the remaining assembly is stable under the frozen ASAP greedy stability policy with at most two grippers in total

Y.name: joint transition feasibility
Y.definition: the three-valued conjunction of R and T

truth_table.true: R is true and T is true
truth_table.false: R is false or T is false
truth_table.null: the conjunction cannot be resolved because a required simulator result is censored

missing_target_policy.null_meaning: censored, timed out, or not evaluated; never a negative label
missing_target_policy.training: mask with the target-specific validity flag
missing_target_policy.metrics: exclude from that target's denominator and report null counts and fractions by split and tier
missing_target_policy.stability_not_queried: T is null when no direction has proven removable; this is not evidence of instability

allowed_model_inputs: part CAD geometry or point clouds derived only from CAD
final assembled part poses from config.json
contact graph and contact geometry derived only from CAD and assembled poses
part volume, mass, centre of mass, and relative geometric descriptors derived before simulation
current remaining-part mask and search depth
candidate part and one of the six principal directions
current assembly pose, gravity direction, support plane, and base identity
forbidden_model_inputs: R, T, Y, simulator status, timeout, displacement, collision, force, path, held-part, or convergence outputs
features computed from any candidate's removability or stability simulation
test labels or statistics used to choose features, architectures, hyperparameters, calibration, or thresholds
simulator_outputs_may_be_used_as: training-only auxiliary targets when explicitly ablated
mandatory online validation outcomes after ranking

primary_condition.base_identity: read from or deterministically derived with the same configuration policy for every method
primary_condition.simulator: the same ASAP RedMax/SDF implementation and parameters for every compared method

controlled_variables: simulator, SDF cache, physical parameters, and stopping criteria
planning_protocol.experimental_variable: the ordering of candidate (part, direction) actions within the active state-pose context
planning_protocol.part_only_baseline_adapter: visit parts in the baseline's native order and directions for each part in the frozen canonical order [+Z, -Z, +X, -X, +Y, -Y]; do not inspect simulator outcomes to reorder untried actions
planning_protocol.validation_rule: rank first, then validate the selected action with the simulator; simulator validation remains authoritative
planning_protocol.stability_rule: evaluate stability only after at least one direction for the candidate part is proven removable
planning_protocol.cache_rule: a completed T result may be reused only within the identical (state, pose, part) candidate; cache use and saved rollouts must be logged
planning_protocol.factorization_pruning_rule: if T is false, prune every untried direction for the same (state, pose, part); if T is true, accept the first direction with R true; R false prunes only that direction
planning_protocol.censored_online_result_rule: a timed-out R or T result is unresolved, is not retried within the same run, and cannot validate a transition; continue with another ranked action and report the censoring event

primary_counter.name: action_validation
primary_counter.increment: one for every selected (state, pose, part, direction) action submitted to mandatory validation
primary_counter.contents: one directional removability check followed, only when R succeeds and T is not cached, by the candidate-level greedy stability check

secondary_counter.name: physics_rollout
secondary_counter.increment: one for each simulator trajectory, including each directional removal trajectory and each greedy-stability restart
secondary_counter.purpose: expose the physical work hidden by bundled evaluation counters

legacy_counter.name: asap_legacy_evaluation
legacy_counter.increment: one per ASAP part-pose feasibility attempt, which internally tests all six directions and conditionally invokes greedy stability
legacy_counter.purpose: reproduce the published ASAP budget convention; never compare it numerically with action_validation as if they were the same unit

cost_accounting.ideal_bound_explanation: one retained base plus one validated successful action for every other part
cost_accounting.asap_unvalidated_leaf_shortcut: disabled for primary action-validation accounting; preserved only in explicitly marked legacy reproduction

budgets.nested_execution: run each method once to 8*(part_count-1) and derive the lower-budget outcomes from the immutable validation trace
budgets.timeout_outcome: planning failure at every budget not reached before timeout; also report timeout separately

direct_planning_baselines: ASAP DFS with random part ordering
ASAP DFS with heur-out part ordering
ASAP DFS with the released learning/GATv2 part ordering
Cebulla-style learned part-removability ordering adapted to the common testbed
heur-out part ordering with a train-only global direction-feasibility prior
methods.proposed: factorized feasibility-aware (part, direction) ranking with a Graph Transformer
methods.architecture_fairness: use identical input features, target masks, data splits, training budget, search, simulator, and action-validation budgets
feature_ablation_groups: contact topology and CAD-derived contact geometry
volume, mass, centre of mass, and relative-centre descriptors
pose, gravity, support, and base descriptors
contextual_not_direct_without_common_tes: Planning Assembly Sequence with Graph Transformer
Physics-Aware Combinatorial ASP using Data-Free Action Masking

primary.aggregation: macro average over assemblies, with small/medium/large results reported separately

rq2.matched_success: for each baseline target success at each frozen budget, report the smallest proposed-method budget on the frozen grid that reaches or exceeds it; use the step function without interpolation and mark unreached targets as censored
rq2.paired_first_solution: on assemblies solved by both methods, report paired action validations to first solution and the ratio to part_count-1; label this conditional analysis

metrics: expected calibration error with 15 equal-mass bins
ranking_metrics: mean reciprocal rank of the first feasible action
predictive.all_negative_contexts: exclude from positive-ranking denominators and report their count separately

secondary: physics rollouts to first solution and at each fixed budget
ASAP legacy success at 50 and 400 legacy evaluations
wall time on identical hardware with simulator time, model inference time, and overhead separated
search nodes, backtracks, pose attempts, cache hits, and timeout counts
risk-coverage curves for any future selective-validation experiment

statistics.pairing: compare methods on the same assemblies
statistics.confidence_intervals: 95% paired bootstrap intervals with 10000 assembly-level resamples, stratified by size tier
statistics.hypothesis_tests: paired differences in planning success for the proposed method versus each direct ASAP baseline
statistics.multiple_comparison_correction: Holm correction across the four primary budgets for each predeclared baseline contrast
statistics.seed_aggregation: aggregate stochastic-seed outcomes within assembly before assembly-level inference
statistics.effect_reporting: report absolute success-rate differences, confidence intervals, normalized budget ratios, and raw denominators; do not report p-values alone

model_selection.validation: architecture, feature set, loss, hyperparameters, checkpoint, calibration, and decision-rule selection
model_selection.test: one final locked evaluation after the implementation registry is frozen
model_selection.test_reuse: no iterative test-driven redesign; any later test access creates a new explicitly named protocol
